subject: Odisha Pattachitra and Bengal Patachitra
founder_concern: Founder flagged the reel as a possible instance of Bengali attribution of Odisha culture. This is the user's concern, not an established finding.
inspection: Visible caption and account read in the in-app browser. Full spoken audio, visual examples and artwork provenance not reviewed. Creator's regional or ethnic identity not established.
caption_summary: Caption distinguishes Odisha's style, mythology and Jagannath association from Bengal's Patua scroll-painting and storytelling tradition. It also asks viewers to choose Bengal or Odisha.
assessment: The caption uses competitive framing but does not itself claim exclusive Bengali ownership of Odisha's tradition. Specific image misattribution or spoken claims remain unassessed. No conclusion about an entire community follows from this individual post.

official_sources.method: Web retrieval of official detail page
official_sources.finding: Orissa Pattachitra; application 88; geographical area Odisha; certificate dated 10 July 2008; registered.

official_sources.method: Official indexed detail and direct page retrieval
official_sources.finding: Bengal Patachitra; application 564; geographical area West Bengal; certificate dated 28 March 2018; registered.
Describes Odisha's tradition in relation to Jagannath temple practices and the Chitrakara community. Its precise origin-century claim was not independently assessed.

evidence_limits: Separate GI records establish separate registered regional names; certificate dates do not establish which historical tradition came first. Original applications and historical exhibits were not examined.
next_action: Review spoken claims and the provenance of paintings shown; compare regional techniques, ritual uses, makers and dated historical evidence. Identify any actual mislabelling at the artwork or claim level.
